question_text: A café owner reviews four decisions: a new menu item, a delivery app partnership, a social media campaign, and the prices on the menu. Which one is the only one that produces revenue?
hint: Only one element of the marketing mix produces revenue. The others represent costs.

options.option_explanation: A menu item is part of the product. All elements other than price represent costs to the organization.
A delivery partnership is a channel decision. It represents a cost, not revenue.
Correct. Price is the only element in the marketing mix that produces revenue.
A campaign is promotion. All other elements represent costs to the organization.

question_text: A company's costs mean it cannot charge less than $20 for a product. Research shows customers will not pay more than $35 for it. What sets the $35 limit?
hint: One factor sets the lower limit and another sets the upper limit.
correct_answer_citation: Week 08 · External Factors: The Market and Demand

options.option_explanation: Costs set the lower limit, the absolute floor for price. Here that is the $20.

options.option_text: Fixed costs that do not vary with sales
options.option_explanation: Fixed costs are part of total costs, and costs set the floor. They do not set what customers will pay.
An objective guides the initial pricing range. It does not decide what customers are willing to pay.

options.option_text: The market sets the upper limit
options.option_explanation: Correct. While costs set the lower limit, the market sets the upper limit.

question_text: Before designing a new e-bike, a Montréal company asks riders what they value and what that is worth to them. It then sets a target price and designs the bike to meet it. Which approach is this?
hint: The company started with the buyers, not with its costs.

options.option_explanation: Cost-based pricing starts from the product and its costs. This company started with what riders value.
Correct. The company assesses customer needs and value perceptions first, and uses them as the key to pricing.
Competition-based pricing looks at competitors' strategies, prices, costs, and offerings. This company asked riders.
Current profit maximization is a marketing objective. The question asks which pricing approach the company used.

question_text: A new gym in Laval compares its offer with nearby rival gyms. It finds members would get more value from it, with longer hours and newer equipment. Using competition-based pricing, what can the gym do?
hint: Think about what greater value allows.

options.option_text: Match the lowest price among its rivals
options.option_explanation: The gym's offer provides greater value, so it does not need to match the lowest price.

options.option_text: Ignore rival prices, since its value is higher
options.option_explanation: Competition-based pricing sets prices based on competitors. Consumers judge value from the prices competitors charge.

options.option_text: Justify a higher price than its rivals
options.option_explanation: Correct. If the offer provides greater value, a higher price can be justified.

options.option_text: Set its price at the floor its costs allow
options.option_explanation: Costs set the lower limit, but nothing here requires pricing at the floor. Greater value can justify more.

question_text: A company plans to launch a new product with market-skimming pricing. Which situation would make that plan a poor choice?
hint: Look at what must be true for a high price to hold.

options.option_text: Its quality and image support a high price
options.option_explanation: Product quality and image must support the high price, so this helps skimming.

options.option_text: Rivals could easily enter and undercut it
options.option_explanation: Correct. Competitors should not be able to easily enter the market and undercut the high price.

options.option_text: It expects fewer but more profitable sales
options.option_explanation: That is what skimming is meant to produce: fewer but more profitable sales.

options.option_text: It will skim revenues layer by layer
options.option_explanation: Skimming maximum revenues layer by layer is the definition of the strategy, not a problem with it.

question_text: A printer maker sells its printers at a low price. It earns most of its profit on ink cartridges that only work in its own printers. Which strategy is this?
hint: The cartridges must be used along with the main product.

options.option_explanation: Optional products are accessories a buyer may choose. Cartridges must be used for the printer to work.
Product line pricing sets the price steps between products in a line. This is about supplies for one main product.
Penetration pricing sets a low initial price to win share quickly. It says nothing about marked-up supplies.
Correct. The main product is priced low, with high markups on the captive supplies that must be used with it.
